content:
Before most people contact a business, they have already read about the problem they want solved. A family comparing homes on Dwarka Expressway and Golf Course Extension Road reads about possession timelines and maintenance charges. A parent in Sector 56 reads about how a coaching institute runs its doubt sessions. A procurement lead at a GCC in Cyber City reads a vendor's guides before booking a demo. Content marketing is the work of answering those questions better than anyone else, so that your business is the one people trust when they are ready to buy. This is what our content team does at TopWebExpert.

What Content Marketing Is, and What It Is Not

It is a planned, steady body of useful material: articles, guides, videos, email newsletters and social posts built around the real questions of your customers. It is not publishing a blog post a day, rewriting competitors' articles or stuffing a city name into every paragraph. Search engines now reward pages written from real experience and penalise mass-produced filler, so we write fewer, deeper pieces with input from the people in your business who know the subject.

Questions Your Buyers Ask Before They Call

We start by collecting the questions your sales team, receptionists and customer support hear every week. Some examples from typical Gurugram businesses:

  • Real estate: "What is the difference between carpet area and super area?" or "What should I check in a builder-buyer agreement?"
  • Hospitals and clinics: "How long is recovery after a knee replacement?" or "Which tests should I do before surgery?"
  • B2B SaaS and IT services: "How do we move from spreadsheets to a CRM without losing data?"
  • D2C brands: "How do I choose the right size?" or "Is this product safe for sensitive skin?"
  • Manufacturing and logistics around Manesar: "What documents does a first-time exporter need?"

Each question becomes a potential piece of content, and we rank them by how often they come up, how close they are to a purchase decision and what already exists online.

The First 90 Days

  1. Weeks 1–2: Audit and interviews. We review your existing website, social channels and analytics, and interview your founders, sales staff or doctors. The interviews can happen at our Sohna Road office in Sector 49, at your premises or over a call.
  2. Weeks 3–4: Strategy and calendar. Keyword and question research, a list of priority topics, a content calendar for the quarter and an agreed tone of voice.
  3. Weeks 5–12: Production. Writing, editing, design and publishing on an agreed schedule, alongside updates to existing pages that are close to ranking but underperforming.
  4. Week 13: Review. A report on what was published, what is gaining traction and what we will change in the next quarter.

Who Writes, and Who Checks

Every piece goes through a clear editorial chain: a writer drafts from an outline and your expert's input, an editor checks structure, facts and readability, and a subject expert on your side approves it before it goes live. Where AI tools help with research or outlines, a human writes and fact-checks the final text.

Some industries need extra care. Medical content should be reviewed by a qualified doctor, and we name the reviewer on the page. Real estate project content must show the RERA registration number where a registered project is promoted. Advertising claims should follow ASCI guidelines. We flag these requirements up front rather than leaving you exposed.

Formats We Produce

  • Long-form guides
  • Blog articles
  • Service and landing page copy
  • Email newsletters
  • LinkedIn posts and articles
  • Short video scripts
  • Case study write-ups from your own data
  • Downloadable checklists
  • Hindi and Hinglish social content

Our working tools include Google Search Console, Google Analytics 4, Ahrefs or Semrush for research, Grammarly and plagiarism checkers for editing, Canva and Figma for visuals, and WordPress or your existing CMS for publishing.

How We Report Progress, Honestly

Content marketing is slow. New articles often take several months to rank, and we will not promise traffic or lead numbers up front. What we do report every month is what was published, which pages are gaining impressions and clicks in Search Console, which topics bring enquiries through your forms or WhatsApp, and what we plan to change as a result. You see the raw data, not a slide of vanity metrics.

Rights to the Content

Everything we write and design for you belongs to you once invoiced work is paid for, including drafts, images we create and the content calendar. Stock images and fonts are licensed properly, and every article is original. If you stop working with us, the content stays on your website and in your accounts.

What You Need to Provide

  • Time with at least one subject expert each month, even 30 minutes on a call.
  • Access to your website CMS, Google Search Console and Analytics.
  • Product details, pricing policies and any brand guidelines.
  • One person who approves content within an agreed turnaround.

Habits That Waste a Content Budget

  • Publishing many thin posts instead of a few thorough ones.
  • Creating near-identical pages for every locality or city with only the name changed.
  • Writing only about the company and never about the customer's problem.
  • Never updating old articles that are close to ranking.
  • Judging results after four weeks and stopping before the work has had time to work.

When Content Marketing Will Not Help You Yet

If you need sales this month, paid ads or direct outreach will act faster. If your website is slow, broken on mobile or has no clear way to enquire, fix that first, or new content will not convert. And if no one in the business can spare time to share expertise, the content will stay generic, which is exactly what search engines and readers now ignore.

Content Marketing FAQs

How long before we see results?

Expect early signs, such as rising impressions in Search Console, within a few months, and meaningful enquiries over a longer period. It depends on your competition, your site's history and how consistently content is published.

How is pricing decided?

It depends on the number and depth of pieces each month, the formats, research needs, design work and whether you need Hindi content. After a free consultation we send a fixed monthly or project quote.

Can you write about technical or medical subjects?

Yes, with your experts' input. We interview them, draft from their answers and have them approve the final version.

Will you post on our social media too?

We can plan and create social posts from the same content and schedule them, or hand them to your in-house team.

Do we need a local agency for this?

Not necessarily, but being based in Gurgaon helps. We can visit your site, interview your team in person and understand local buyers first-hand.
